name: Lumen Circuit
summary: Rotate an optical network so a living beam preserves negation, uncertainty and quantity. Light follows the actual conduit geometry; a different path changes the message.
algorithm: A five-by-five network contains straight and elbow conduits. Rotations change connected ports. Trace a source from west to east with a visited port-state set and a 100-hop cap. Semantic gates on visited cells toggle polarity, mark uncertainty or increment quantity. A receiver accepts only the complete target tuple and a connected physical route. Solvable layouts are generated by constructing a non-self-intersecting route first, placing its gates, and scrambling rotations afterwards.
session: Twelve chambers, initially one transformation and generous geometry, then multiple gates, longer paths and distracting branches. No timer. Three discharged pulses at a wrong receiver lose the current chamber; restart preserves the checkpoint and changes no learning estimate until a new assessed pulse.
controls: Tap/click a conduit to rotate clockwise. Arrow keys move a visible grid focus; Space rotates. Enter or the Pulse button launches an assessed trace. Undo restores the previous rotation. A hint reveals one needed conduit and marks this chamber assisted.
art: Obsidian optical instruments, brushed copper sockets, deep teal mist, luminous ivory light and tiny prism caustics. The board is physical and central, with animated light packets travelling along live segments. Title art is an original crystal aperture; essential gate symbols are visual, with optional names in help.
feel: Immediate socket rotation, a short settling spring, 140 ms pulse travel between cells, warm chord on faithful arrival and a soft fractured tone on dissipation. The player should inspect a route and feel the physical consequence of a missing qualifier.

name: Drift Archive
summary: Cross a shifting archipelago while holding the order and constraints of a message in memory. You choose the route and where to leave limited memory anchors.
algorithm: Generate a connected island graph on a five-by-five lattice. Pick a start, an ordered two-to-four destination sequence and one forbidden island outside that sequence. A breadth-first reachability check validates every destination after exclusions. The message is visible during preparation, then fades when travel begins. Tap a neighboring island or use arrows to move. Wind changes traversal speed, never semantic correctness. Entering a destination out of order or the forbidden location is an assessed constraint error; ordinary travel is not evidence.
session: Eight routes introduce order, then negative constraints, longer sequences, optional anchors and changing graph edges. Three constraint errors fail a route, not the whole career. Replay reshuffles topology and waypoint order. Completed routes checkpoint immediately; viewing the source again marks assistance.
controls: Tap adjacent islands to travel; arrows select cardinal neighbors and Space confirms focused travel. Pin toggles a memory anchor on the focused island; capacity two. Peek briefly returns the source and records support. Enter starts a prepared route.
art: Floating indigo islands, rose-gold dawn, paper-sail couriers, layered clouds, hanging roots and flowing wind ribbons. Depth comes from island silhouettes and moving parallax, not panels of text. Destination glyphs are distinct in shape as well as color.
feel: The courier eases into a gust and glides to the selected island over 0.45–0.9 seconds. A soft landing ring confirms arrival; wrong order produces a spatial echo of the missed waypoint. The mood is deliberate exploration with memory pressure, not a reflex test.

name: Counterpoint
summary: Conduct overlapping speaker channels. Hold a complete unit, route its term into the right target-language receiver, and release at the right moment without clipping the source.
algorithm: Two channels grow into three. Each speaker emits a bounded packet with a known English term, a complete source unit, a target-language term from the reused knowledge and an arrival deadline. Packet charge reaches complete after its declared duration. A selected channel can be routed to one of the displayed receiver lanes, then committed. Early commit clips the unit; wrong receiver changes the term; overflow loses the packet. Clarification freezes a packet briefly but is logged as assistance. Fixed-step scheduling and stable packet IDs resolve simultaneous arrivals before player commits.
session: Six movements of 45 seconds, with a finite target number of faithful deliveries and a three-error recovery budget. Each movement changes term mix, channel concurrency, receiver positions and source duration, so a fixed tapping pattern is not a solution. No recorded speech or listening proficiency is claimed from musical cues.
controls: Tap a speaker to select it, tap a target receiver to route, then tap Release. Number keys 1–3 select speakers, left/right choose a receiver, Space releases, C clarifies. A visible charge ring and shape-coded channel ribbon communicate completeness without long text.
art: A midnight concert hall of curved brass channels, coral and lavender signals, silhouetted speakers and a reflective stage. The world resembles an instrument being played. Payload terms are concise in-world labels; full definitions are optional help.
feel: Commit is percussive and immediate. Complete packets resolve into harmonic chords; a clipped turn leaves an audible rest and a broken ribbon. The interaction should feel like balancing simultaneous musical lines while protecting the identity of each voice.

name: Marginfall
summary: Traverse a folding world where a short instruction changes the viable route. Read intent ahead of movement, preserve a negative or conditional constraint, and use a reversible air dash to recover.
algorithm: A fixed-step platform body owns position, velocity, grounded state and one air dash. Gravity, coyote time and buffered jumps make input reliable. Each chamber generates a solvable left-to-right platform route with two physically traversable branches; a brief specifies the allowed crest, prohibited color/shape or required checkpoint order. Physics collisions happen before checkpoint assessment; falling is a motor error and produces no language evidence. Only passage through an explicit semantic gate assesses whether the instruction was preserved.
session: Ten chambers across a continuous ink canyon. Early chambers teach jump and landing safely; later ones add a dash, moving ledges, conditional gates and route planning. A fall returns to the last stable ledge. Three semantic gate errors reset the chamber. Motor difficulty and semantic evidence remain separate.
controls: A/D or arrows move, Space/W jumps, Shift dashes once in the air. On touch, three large controls provide left, right and jump; a separate dash button appears after onboarding. Tap controls and keyboard share the same held-state input. R resets the current chamber without awarding evidence.
art: An ivory and ultramarine paper landscape with sculpted black silhouettes, ink blooms, floating margins and warm amber checkpoints. The player is a luminous brushstroke with a short trail. World geometry, movement and shadows dominate; the instruction is a single short line.
feel: Responsive acceleration, 110 ms coyote time, 120 ms jump buffer, a 140 ms dash and forgiving edge contacts. Camera framing shows the next decision before it becomes a jump. A failed jump should invite another attempt, while a wrong interpretation should visibly change the gate.

name: Common Ground
summary: Coordinate a living city of encounters, one tactical turn at a time. Choose which voice to serve, preserve the intended recipient and constraints, and clarify missing meaning rather than invent it.
algorithm: A seven-by-seven walkable city grid contains walls, speakers, recipients and scheduled encounter requests. The interpreter has three movement points and two bounded message slots. Collecting a request stores its known semantic fields; an unknown field remains unknown until clarification at its speaker costs an action. A relay assesses recipient, field completeness and preserved meaning, then updates the encounter. NPC intentions are telegraphed before the turn advances. A seeded generator validates routes and schedules feasible deadlines; no real legal or clinical decision is made by the player.
session: Six districts, each a finite twelve-turn encounter schedule with increasing concurrent responsibilities. The player needs a threshold of faithful resolutions and must avoid three unclarified or misdirected relays. Earlier skill handoffs matter: qualifiers, memory anchors, queue coordination and planning ahead. A new run changes city layout, encounter order and traffic.
controls: Tap reachable tiles or use arrows to move. Space interacts with the adjacent focused person; Clarify resolves missing information at its source; Relay delivers the selected message to an adjacent recipient. Tab changes carried message; End turn resolves telegraphed intentions. Touch controls duplicate every action.
art: A lantern-lit terracotta and jade city, isometric building caps, rain-slick paths, small expressive residents and visible arcs between voices. Meaning is carried as compact symbol packets. The tactical plan is legible from shapes and positions before reading optional detail.
feel: Deliberate, reversible movement within a turn, readable intent previews, a satisfying shared light when an encounter resolves, and a brief pause for the recipient response. Pressure comes from competing human needs and limited attention, not a countdown or a wall of choices.
